channel_findings.constants: Text on 20 of 20: heavy condensed all-caps sans, white fill, thick black outline, no box, no highlighted word. US state map as base on 19 of 20 (exception: globe, n=10). Saturated gradients in magenta/pink or red/orange against cyan/blue; dark navy or black surround. Arrows on 13 of 20 (n=3,5,7,8,10,11,12,13,15,16,17,18,19), white with black outline. No border, logo, channel mark or host on any thumbnail.
channel_findings.host_treatment: No host on any of the 20. Face present on 0 of 20; no person appears at all. Lighting, cut-out, size and placement cannot be measured. This contradicts the lead's premise that Ryan Hall puts his face on forecast thumbnails. Confirm with the orchestrator before any face rule is taken from this channel.
channel_findings.text_rules: Words: 2 words on 16 of 20, 3 words on 4 of 20 (n=8,10,11,13). Lines: 2 lines on 17 of 20, 1 line on 3 (n=5,6,10). Case: upper on 20 of 20. Colour: white fill with black outline on 20 of 20. Position: top-left on 17 of 20, top-centre on 2 (n=6,10), left-middle on 1 (n=8). Highlight: none. Biggest line roughly 18 to 33 percent of frame height (visual estimate). Title link: text repeats the title's keyword on 8 of 20 (n=1,2,4,8,14,16,17,20) and adds a second idea on 12 (see per-thumb title_link).
channel_findings.popular_vs_latest: Popular (n=1 to 10): median 3,300,000 views. Latest (n=11 to 20): median 2,350,000 views. Popular set uses 'WINTER PREDICTION' or 'winter' text on n=1,2,4 and 'LOTS OF SNOW' on n=8; 3 of 10 are 1-line. Latest set uses all 2-line text (10 of 10), 8 of 10 arrows (n=11,12,13,15,16,17,18,19), and more change or question words (NEW FORECAST, BIG CHANGE, WHAT'S THIS, IT KEEPS GOING). The best latest thumbnail (n=20, 7.0M) has no arrow and reuses the popular winter text.
channel_findings.top3: n=1 (13.0M), n=2 (7.2M), n=20 (7.0M). All three: 'WINTER PREDICTION' text (n=2 is 'WINTER PREDICTION' too), 2 lines, top-left, white with black outline; full-bleed US map in magenta and cyan; no arrow; no face; no badge. The shared element is the text and map gradient, not an arrow or a person.
transfer: Headline: 2 words, all caps, white with thick black outline, top-left, 2 lines at about 30% of frame height. Evidence: n=1, 2, 20 (13.0M, 7.2M, 7.0M) all match; 16 of 20 use 2 words.

Keyword: pair a generic forecast word with the topic word, e.g. 'WINTER PREDICTION'. Evidence: n=1, 2, 4, 20 all use it; the 4 of them range from 4.0M to 13.0M views. For storms, the same pattern would be '[STORM] PREDICTION' or '[STORM] FORECAST'.
Background: full-bleed US map with one saturated gradient (magenta vs cyan), dark edges, no arrow. Evidence: n=1, 2, 20 are all this; 19 of 20 are map-based.

Arrows: keep arrows to one per thumbnail and only when the title promises a change. Evidence: n=3, 5, 7 use two arrows and sit at 4.1M, 3.7M, 2.9M; the top 3 use none. Eight latest thumbnails use one arrow each and the best latest (n=20) has none.

Face: this set has no face, so no rule about presenter placement can be drawn from it. Test a presenter cut-out on the T1 layout (n=1, 2, 20) as a split test against the no-face baseline; do not assume a face lifts clicks from this evidence.
weak: n=11 'IT KEEPS GOING' (0.93M, lowest in channel sample): grey base and rainbow stripe give low contrast, the arrow points at a band with no place or number named.
n=6 'FRESH DATA' (2.9M): process label, not a claim; the text names no finding, so the viewer gets no reason to open the video beyond the title.
n=10 'OUT OF HAND' (2.8M): abstract globe with no place or number; the arrow points at a glow the viewer cannot place.
